note.headline: Stocks rip, curve flattens, oil falls six percent: risk on without a clean story
note.standfirst: The S&P gained 2.35% and the Russell 2000 gained 3.15%, with breadth running 21 advancers to 5 decliners, while the long end sold off faster than the front end flattened the curve further. Positioning now has to reconcile a risk-on tape with crude down six percent and the VIX dropping 22% in a single session.
takeaways: Equities rallied broadly, with small caps and tech both outrunning the S&P and breadth confirming the move at 4.2 to 1.
The curve flattened again, 2s10s down 3bp to 35bp, even as long yields held near cycle highs.
Crude fell hard, WTI off 4.60% and Brent off 6.09%, while natural gas jumped 6.80%, a split energy tape that argues against a single demand narrative.
Volatility compressed across the board, VIX down 22.31% and MOVE down 7.32%, with credit spreads tightening in sympathy.
note.desk_view:
The session confirms that the October growth scare has not left a mark on risk appetite. AMD and AVGO led single names, up 13.26% and 8.78%, and the move was not confined to megacap tech: Russell 2000 up 3.15%, mid caps up 3.13%, industrials up 3.82%. Breadth at 4.2 to 1 with dispersion of 3.4 says this was a broad bid, not a handful of names dragging the index. Credit did its part too, HYG up 0.36%, EMB up 0.63%, both tightening on a day equities ripped. That is the consensus trade working as designed.

The level that decides whether this holds is 10-year yields. UST10Y closed 4.86%, up only 2bp on the day versus a 5bp move in 2s, so the curve flattened on short-end weakness, not long-end conviction. If 10s push back toward the recent high with the front end still backing up, the flattening becomes a policy story rather than a risk-on one, and equities will have to decide whether they can rally through it again. Gold up 1.84% to 4149.80 alongside the equity rally is the one piece that does not fit cleanly. Watch whether gold keeps bid on days stocks rally. That combination, risk-on equities and a bid for gold, is not free money, it is a market hedging two different outcomes at once.
watching: Whether UST10Y breaks back above 4.86% or holds, deciding if the flattening is policy-driven or risk-driven.
Oil's six percent Brent drop, whether it extends or reverses, and what that implies for the energy sector laggards.
Gold's bid against a risk-on tape, a divergence worth resolving before extrapolating the rally.
VIX follow-through below 20 after today's 22.31% drop, confirming whether the vol crush has legs into next week.
note.equities:
All six major US benchmarks closed higher, led by the Nasdaq 100 at +3.40% and the Russell 2000 at +3.15%, with the Dow trailing the pack at +2.15%. Sector rotation favored cyclicals and growth together: technology up 3.73%, industrials up 3.82%, consumer discretionary up 2.92%, while staples and energy lagged at +0.90% and +0.52%. That is a rotation into everything except the defensive and commodity-linked sleeves.

Breadth confirmed the rally, 21 advancers against 5 decliners, a 4.2 ratio that leaves little room to call this narrow. AMD and AVGO topped the leader board, up 13.26% and 8.78%, both semiconductor names moving well ahead of NVDA, which fell 4.27% and sat alone among large tech as a laggard. Energy majors CVX and XOM also lagged, down 0.86% and 0.69%, consistent with the day's crude selloff. Dispersion of 3.4 says the gains were not uniform even inside a broad advance.
note.rates:
The curve flattened again: 2s10s down 3bp to 35bp, 5s30s down 4bp to 62bp. Levels stayed elevated across the board, 2-year at 4.51%, 10-year at 4.86%, 30-year at 5.26%, with the front end bearing the brunt of the day's move and the long end comparatively anchored.

Breakeven data in the pack is dated November 6 and off-session, so no fresh read on inflation expectations today. The MOVE index fell 7.32%, consistent with the broader vol compression, and sits well above its own year-to-date low even after the drop. No auction results are in today's pack.
note.credit: Credit traded with the equity tape, not against it. LQD rose 0.13%, HYG rose 0.36%, JNK rose 0.33%, and EMB rose 0.63%, a tightening move across investment grade, high yield and EM sovereign risk simultaneously. Leveraged loans added 0.20%. Nothing here argues for stress. The tone is calm and the move is in line with equity beta, not ahead of it.
note.fx: The dollar index fell 0.61% to 101.68, with the move uneven across G10. EUR/USD was little changed, down 0.01%, while GBP/USD fell 0.11% and AUD/USD dropped 0.04%, so the DXY decline was not a clean broad-dollar story. USD/CNY fell 0.39% to a session low per the extremes list, and USD/INR fell 0.57%. EM carry currencies, USD/MXN, USD/BRL and USD/TRY, were flat on the day per the pack, with TRY itself printing a high.
note.commodities: Energy diverged sharply from the rest of the complex. WTI fell 4.60% and Brent fell 6.09%, while natural gas rose 6.80%, so this was not a broad energy selloff, it was crude specific. Precious metals rallied together with the equity tape: gold up 1.84% to 4149.80, silver up 3.21%, platinum up 2.68%, palladium up 2.11%. Copper rose 2.55%, consistent with the risk-on read elsewhere. Aluminium fell 1.44%, bucking the industrial metals move. Agricultural prices were soft across the board, wheat, corn, soybeans, coffee, cocoa and sugar all lower.
note.volatility: The vol complex collapsed. VIX fell 22.31% to 19.92, VIX9D fell 26.86% to 19.88, and VIX3M fell 15.24% to 20.85, flattening the term structure's recent steepness. VVIX dropped 19.28% to 98.43. SKEW is dated November 6 and off-session, so tail pricing has not been refreshed today. The cost of protection fell hard and fast, the kind of move that typically follows a sharp reduction in realized volatility rather than leads it.
note.digital: Digital assets were broadly flat to modestly higher, a muted response given the equity rally. Bitcoin rose 0.47% to 74,931.40, Ether rose 0.28%, Solana rose 0.14%, while XRP fell 1.39%. The beta to risk that showed up in small caps and credit did not show up here. Crypto sat out today's move.
note.international: European bourses closed broadly higher ahead of the US open, with the FTSE MIB up 2.69% and the EURO STOXX 50 up 1.94%, a tone that carried through to New York. Asia was split: the Nikkei rose 2.33% and TAIEX jumped 4.94%, while the Hang Seng fell 0.13% and the KOSPI fell 0.81%. That divergence, a strong Japan and Taiwan session against a soft Hong Kong and Korea print, handed New York a mixed regional setup rather than a clean global risk-on signal.
note.correlation:
Today's cross-asset pattern was mostly coherent: equities up, credit spreads tighter, vol down, copper up, all consistent with a single risk-on regime. The outlier is gold, up 1.84% on a day stocks rallied hard, alongside a crude market that fell sharply for reasons the rest of the tape does not explain. That is two assets refusing to fit the dominant story.

A break in the usual equity-vol inverse relationship would be the signal to watch for next. Today that relationship held tightly, VIX down 22% as SPX rose 2.35%. If VIX stops falling on green equity days, or starts rising with equities still up, that decorrelation would mean the vol compression was a one-off unwind rather than a durable repricing of risk.
